answers.why: Paul's chain concerns the hope of his nation, Israel.
Those descended from Israel trace their ancestry to Jacob, paralleling Abraham's seed in the next verse.
Israel here names the collective to which not all physical descendants belong.
Israel is contrasted with the Gentiles and described as pursuing righteousness through the law.
Moses' words address Israel collectively as those provoked by another nation.
The sentence explicitly describes Israel as a disobedient and contradicting people.
Elijah complains against the people who killed God's prophets and destroyed his altars.
Israel comprises the elect who obtained what they sought and the rest who were hardened.
Partial hardening affects Israel collectively until the fullness of the Gentiles enters.
All Israel is a collective whose sins God promises to remove in the following verse.
Israel according to the flesh comprises those who eat sacrifices and share in the altar.
The Israel of God is a community receiving Paul's blessing of peace and mercy.
